equity_risk_premium.name: equity_risk_premium
equity_risk_premium.source: Aswath Damodaran - Implied Equity Risk Premium, United States
equity_risk_premium.rationale: MATURE-MARKET ERP ONLY; country risk is added separately, so a country-weighted ERP here would double count. KNOWN MISMATCH: this is the January 2026 reading paired with an August 2026 risk-free rate. Damodaran recomputes the implied ERP from the prevailing risk-free rate each month, so the two inputs describe different market states. Replace with the latest monthly publication.

unlevered_industry_beta.name: unlevered_industry_beta
unlevered_industry_beta.source: Aswath Damodaran - US Industry Betas, Business & Consumer Services, unlevered beta corrected for cash
unlevered_industry_beta.rationale: Bottom-up industry beta rather than Uber's single-stock regression beta. Business & Consumer Services is a better economic proxy for a platform-based mobility and delivery marketplace than asset-heavy Transportation. Damodaran reports 0.77 unlevered, 0.81 corrected for cash. The engine relevers via Hamada. The industry choice is itself the judgement here: a Software (Internet) or Transportation classification would produce a materially different beta.

debt_spread.name: debt_spread
debt_spread.source: Aswath Damodaran - Ratings, Interest Coverage Ratios and Default Spread
debt_spread.rationale: Spread over the risk-free rate, not the full yield; the engine computes (risk_free + spread). Damodaran's January 2026 spread for Baa2/BBB large non-financial service firms is 1.11%. Uber is rated BBB+ by S&P but the table has no BBB+ bucket, so BBB is used as a conservative and reproducible proxy: a wider spread raises WACC and lowers value.

country_risk_premium.name: country_risk_premium
country_risk_premium.source: analyst judgment, weighted on Uber FY2024 Note 13 geographic revenue
country_risk_premium.rationale: Weighted on the Note 2 geographic revenue mix the pipeline selects and prints: US&CAN 23,618 (54%), LatAm 2,795 (6%), EMEA 12,529 (28%), APAC 5,036 (11%). Two judgements build this number and neither is disclosed. FIRST, which revenue carries country risk: LatAm and APAC are emerging at 17% of revenue, US&CAN is mature at zero by convention, and EMEA at 28% is not disaggregated, so the non-mature share of it is unobservable and half is assumed - giving a 31% weight. SECOND, the premium that weight multiplies: an assumed 2% for the emerging bucket, derived from no disclosure. 31% x 2% = 0.0062; the committed 0.0064 is retained because it is within rounding of the recomputation and is the figure every run so far was made on. THIS IS DIRECTIONAL, NOT NEUTRAL: a higher CRP raises the cost of equity and lowers value, so understating it overstates the company. SUPERSEDED: an earlier version of this rationale opened with ASSUMED ZERO above a non-zero value and weighted on the Note 13 split (US 48%, UK 19%, all other 32%) that the pipeline no longer selects. The number survived the change of source data - 0.32 x 2% and 0.31 x 2% agree to within rounding - which is why it is kept rather than restated.

country_risk_premium.name: country_risk_premium
country_risk_premium.source: analyst judgment, weighted on the FY2025 two-bucket geographic revenue disclosure
country_risk_premium.rationale: Same method as the other filers, on far less disclosure. DoorDash reports only two buckets: United States 11,460 (83.5%) and International 2,257 (16.5%). The entire non-US bucket is undisaggregated, so the half-non-mature assumption applied to Uber's EMEA is applied to all of it here: an 8.2% weight against an assumed 2% emerging-bucket premium gives 0.0016. This is the weakest CRP of the three by disclosure quality. The direction of the likely error is that International is MORE mature than assumed - it is Canada, Australia, Wolt's Nordic and European markets and Deliveroo's UK and European markets, with Mexico the main emerging exposure - so this probably overstates the premium, which understates value and is the conservative direction.
